description:
Design an 8-bit Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) that can perform the following operations based on the provided control signal: 
1. Addition (op = 00)
2. Subtraction (op = 01)
3. AND operation (op = 10)
4. OR operation (op = 11)

The ALU should take two 8-bit inputs `a` and `b`, and a 2-bit control signal `op`, and produce an 8-bit output `result` based on the selected operation. The ALU should also have a carry-out output for the addition and subtraction operations.
code:
module ALU (
    input [7:0] a,
    input [7:0] b,
    input [1:0] op,
    output reg [7:0] result,
    output reg carry_out
);
    
    always @(*) begin
        case (op)
            2'b00: begin // Addition
                {carry_out, result} = a + b;
            end
            2'b01: begin // Subtraction
                {carry_out, result} = a - b;
            end
            2'b10: begin // AND
                result = a & b;
                carry_out = 0; // No carry for AND
            end
            2'b11: begin // OR
                result = a | b;
                carry_out = 0; // No carry for OR
            end
            default: begin
                result = 8'b00000000;
                carry_out = 0;
            end
        endcase
    end
endmodule

Design an echo cancellation system that takes a 1-bit input signal representing the received signal and a 1-bit input signal representing the echo. The system should output a 1-bit signal that represents the canceled echo. The echo cancellation should use a simple finite state machine (FSM) to toggle the output based on the received signal and the echo. The system should operate with a clock input and a reset input.
code:
module echo_cancellation(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input received_signal,
    input echo,
    output reg canceled_signal
);
    reg [1:0] state;

    // State encoding
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, 
              PROCESS = 2'b01, 
              OUTPUT = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            canceled_signal <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (received_signal) begin
                        state <= PROCESS;
                    end
                end
                PROCESS: begin
                    canceled_signal <= received_signal ^ echo; // XOR to cancel echo
                    state <= OUTPUT;
                end
                OUTPUT: begin
                    state <= IDLE; // Return to idle after processing
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Watchdog Timer that resets when a signal is received within a specific timeout period. The timer counts up on each clock cycle and resets if the signal is received before the timer reaches a defined limit. The output should indicate if the timer has expired.
code:
module WatchdogTimer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire signal,
    output reg timer_expired
);
    parameter TIMEOUT = 8'd100; // Set timeout limit
    reg [7:0] count;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            count <= 8'd0;
            timer_expired <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (signal) begin
                count <= 8'd0; // Reset count on signal
                timer_expired <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                count <= count + 1;
                if (count >= TIMEOUT) begin
                    timer_expired <= 1'b1; // Timer expired
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

A 5-bit Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) based CSPRNG that generates pseudo-random numbers. The LFSR should accept a 5-bit seed value and produce a 5-bit random output at each clock cycle. The feedback polynomial used is x^5 + x^2 + 1.
code:
module LFSR_CSPRNG (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [4:0] seed,
    output reg [4:0] random_out
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            random_out <= seed;
        end else begin
            random_out <= {random_out[3:0], (random_out[4] ^ random_out[1])}; // Feedback from bit 4 and bit 2

    end
endmodule

Implement an Adaptive LMS filter in Verilog that takes an input signal and desired signal, adjusts the filter coefficients based on the LMS algorithm, and outputs the filtered signal.
code:
module adaptive_lms_filter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input signed [15:0] x,      // Input signal
    input signed [15:0] d,      // Desired signal
    output reg signed [15:0] y   // Output signal
);
    parameter N = 5;            // Number of taps
    parameter mu = 16'sd1;      // Step size
    reg signed [15:0] w [0:N-1]; // Coefficients
    reg signed [15:0] x_buf [0:N-1]; // Input buffer
    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                w[i] <= 16'sd0; // Initialize weights
                x_buf[i] <= 16'sd0; // Initialize buffer
            end
            y <= 16'sd0; // Initialize output
        end else begin
            // Shift input buffer
            for (i = N-1; i > 0; i = i - 1) begin
                x_buf[i] <= x_buf[i-1];
            end
            x_buf[0] <= x; // New input

            // Calculate output
            y <= 16'sd0;
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                y <= y + (w[i] * x_buf[i]); // Filter output
            end

            // Update weights
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                w[i] <= w[i] + (mu * (d - y) * x_buf[i]); // LMS update
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Implement a simple Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) inference module that performs a single convolution operation on a 3x3 input feature map with a 2x2 filter. The CNN should have an activation function (ReLU) applied to the output. The module will take a clock signal, reset signal, and a valid input signal to initiate the operation. It will output the convolved feature map after processing.
code:
module cnn_inference(  
    input clk,  
    input rst,  
    input valid,  
    input [8*3-1:0] input_map, // 3x3 input feature map  
    input [8*2-1:0] filter,     // 2x2 filter  
    output reg [8*2-1:0] output_map // 2x2 output feature map  
);  
    reg [8*2-1:0] conv_result;  
    integer i, j;  
  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin  
        if (rst) begin  
            output_map <= 0;  
        end else if (valid) begin  
            conv_result = 0;  
            for (i = 0; i < 2; i = i + 1) begin  
                for (j = 0; j < 2; j = j + 1) begin  
                    conv_result[i*8 +: 8] = conv_result[i*8 +: 8] +  
                        (input_map[(i+j)*8 +: 8] * filter[j*8 +: 8]);  
                end  
            end  
            output_map <= (conv_result > 0) ? conv_result : 0; // ReLU activation  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description:
Design a fan speed control system that regulates the speed of a fan based on the temperature input. The fan has three speed settings: OFF, LOW, and HIGH. The system accepts a 2-bit temperature input: 
00 (low temperature), 01 (medium temperature), 10 (high temperature), and 11 (very high temperature). 
The fan should operate as follows:
- Temperature 00: Fan OFF
- Temperature 01: Fan LOW
- Temperature 10: Fan HIGH
- Temperature 11: Fan HIGH
code:
module fan_speed_controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [1:0] temperature,
    output reg [1:0] fan_speed // 00: OFF, 01: LOW, 10: HIGH
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            fan_speed <= 2'b00; // Initial state OFF
        end else begin
            case (temperature)
                2'b00: fan_speed <= 2'b00; // OFF
                2'b01: fan_speed <= 2'b01; // LOW
                2'b10: fan_speed <= 2'b10; // HIGH
                2'b11: fan_speed <= 2'b10; // HIGH
                default: fan_speed <= 2'b00; // Default to OFF
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a DVFS controller that adjusts the voltage and frequency of a processing unit based on the workload. The controller should take the workload as input and output the corresponding frequency and voltage levels. The frequency and voltage should be selected from predefined sets based on the workload ranges.

    input reset,

    output reg [2:0] voltage    // 3-bit voltage output

            frequency <= 3'b000;  
            voltage <= 3'b000;

                    frequency <= 3'b001; // 1 GHz  
                    voltage <= 3'b001;   // 1 V

                4'b0001: begin  
                    frequency <= 3'b010; // 2 GHz

                    frequency <= 3'b100; // 4 GHz  
                    voltage <= 3'b100;   // 1.8 V

                    frequency <= 3'b000;  
                    voltage <= 3'b000;  
                end  
            endcase  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

A UART controller that transmits data serially at a specified baud rate. The controller should accept an 8-bit data input and a transmit enable signal. When the transmit enable signal is high, the controller should begin sending the data bit by bit, starting with the least significant bit (LSB), followed by a stop bit after the entire byte is transmitted. The output should indicate the current bit being transmitted.
code:
module uart_transmitter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    input transmit_en,
    output reg tx,
    output reg busy
);

    reg [3:0] bit_count;  // Counts the number of bits sent
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;  // Holds the data to be sent

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            tx <= 1'b1;  // Idle state
            busy <= 1'b0;
            bit_count <= 4'd0;
            shift_reg <= 8'd0;
        end else if (transmit_en && !busy) begin
            busy <= 1'b1;
            shift_reg <= data_in;
            bit_count <= 4'd0;
            tx <= 1'b0;  // Start bit
        end else if (busy) begin
            if (bit_count < 8) begin
                tx <= shift_reg[bit_count];  // Transmit data bits
                bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
            end else if (bit_count == 8) begin
                tx <= 1'b1;  // Stop bit
                bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
            end else begin
                busy <= 1'b0;  // Transmission complete
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Verilog module that implements a simplified version of the A* search algorithm to find the shortest path on a grid. The input will be the current node position (x, y) and the goal node position (goal_x, goal_y). The output should be the next node to move towards on the path to the goal.
code:
module AStarPathFinder (
    input [4:0] x,         // Current X position (5 bits, max 31)
    input [4:0] y,         // Current Y position (5 bits, max 31)
    input [4:0] goal_x,    // Goal X position (5 bits, max 31)
    input [4:0] goal_y,    // Goal Y position (5 bits, max 31)
    output reg [4:0] next_x, // Next X position
    output reg [4:0] next_y  // Next Y position
);

always @(*) begin
    // Simple heuristic: move towards the goal position
    if (x < goal_x) begin
        next_x = x + 1;  // Move right
    end else if (x > goal_x) begin
        next_x = x - 1;  // Move left
    end else begin
        next_x = x;      // Stay in the same column
    end
    
    if (y < goal_y) begin
        next_y = y + 1;  // Move down
    end else if (y > goal_y) begin
        next_y = y - 1;  // Move up
    end else begin
        next_y = y;      // Stay in the same row
    end
end

endmodule

description:
Design a Verilog module that performs Huffman encoding for a fixed set of input characters. The module should take a 4-bit input representing a character and output a corresponding variable-length encoded binary string based on predefined Huffman codes. The output should be a 12-bit wide signal, where unused bits are filled with zeros. The Huffman codes for the characters A, B, C, D, and E are as follows:
- A: 00
- B: 01
- C: 10
- D: 110
- E: 111
code:
module huffman_encoder (
    input [3:0] char_in,
    output reg [11:0] encoded_out
);

always @(*) begin
    case (char_in)
        4'b0000: encoded_out = 12'b00_000000000; // A
        4'b0001: encoded_out = 12'b01_000000000; // B
        4'b0010: encoded_out = 12'b10_000000000; // C
        4'b0011: encoded_out = 12'b110_00000000; // D
        4'b0100: encoded_out = 12'b111_00000000; // E
        default: encoded_out = 12'b000000000000; // Default case for invalid input
    endcase
end

endmodule

Design a Hamming (7,4) encoder in Verilog. The encoder should take 4 input bits and produce 7 output bits, including 3 parity bits that ensure error detection and correction. The input bits (D[3:0]) should be processed to generate the output bits (Y[6:0]) according to the Hamming code rules.
code:
module hamming_encoder (
    input [3:0] D,
    output reg [6:0] Y

module kalman_filter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [15:0] sensor1,
    input [15:0] sensor2,
    output reg [15:0] estimated_value
);

    reg [15:0] x;     // State estimate
    reg [15:0] p;     // Estimate covariance
    reg [15:0] q;     // Process noise covariance
    reg [15:0] r;     // Measurement noise covariance
    reg [15:0] k;     // Kalman Gain

    initial begin
        x = 16'h0000;  // Initial state estimate
        p = 16'hFFFF;  // Initial covariance
        q = 16'h0001;  // Process noise
        r = 16'h0002;  // Measurement noise
    end

        if (rst) begin
            x <= 16'h0000;
            p <= 16'hFFFF;

            // Prediction Step
            p <= p + q;

            // Measurement Update Step
            k <= p / (p + r);
            x <= x + k * (sensor1 + sensor2)/2 - x; // Average of sensor1 and sensor2
            p <= (16'hFFFF - k) * p; // Update covariance

            estimated_value <= x; // Output the estimated value
        end
    end

description: Design a frequency divider that takes a clock input and outputs a signal that toggles its state every N clock cycles. The value of N should be configurable via a 4-bit input. The output signal should also have the same frequency as the input clock divided by N.

    output reg out          // Output divided clock
);

            out <= 1'b0;

);

module KoggeStoneAdder (

    input [3:0] B,
    output [3:0] SUM,
    output COUT
);
    wire [3:0] P, G, C;
    wire [4:0] C_temp;

    assign G = A & B; // Generate Generate

    assign C_temp[1] = G[0]; // Carry for bit 1
    assign C_temp[2] = G[1] | (P[1] & C_temp[1]); // Carry for bit 2
    assign C_temp[3] = G[2] | (P[2] & C_temp[2]); // Carry for bit 3
    assign C_temp[4] = G[3] | (P[3] & C_temp[3]); // Carry for bit 4 (COUT)

    assign COUT = C_temp[4]; // Final carry out

The output will be the interpolated pixel intensity.

module bilinear_interpolation (
    input [7:0] I00,     // intensity of pixel (0,0)
    input [7:0] I01,     // intensity of pixel (0,1)
    input [7:0] I10,     // intensity of pixel (1,0)
    input [7:0] I11,     // intensity of pixel (1,1)
    input [3:0] x_frac,  // fractional x coordinate (0 to 15)
    input [3:0] y_frac,  // fractional y coordinate (0 to 15)
    output reg [7:0] I_out // interpolated intensity
);

    wire [15:0] I0, I1, I2, I3;
    wire [15:0] x_weight, y_weight;

    assign x_weight = {8'b0, x_frac}; // scale x_frac to 16 bits
    assign y_weight = {8'b0, y_frac}; // scale y_frac to 16 bits

    assign I0 = I00 * (16'hFFFF - x_weight); // weight for I00
    assign I1 = I01 * (16'hFFFF - x_weight); // weight for I01
    assign I2 = I10 * x_weight;               // weight for I10
    assign I3 = I11 * x_weight;               // weight for I11

    always @(*) begin
        I_out = (I0 * (16'hFFFF - y_weight) + I1 * (16'hFFFF - y_weight) +
                 I2 * y_weight + I3 * y_weight) >> 16; // sum and scale back
    end
endmodule

The input will be a 4-bit binary representation of the matrix elements (A, B, C, D) and the output will be a 4-bit binary representation of the elements of the inverse matrix (A_inv, B_inv, C_inv, D_inv).
code:
module matrix_inverse(
    input [3:0] A, // Element A (row 1, column 1)
    input [3:0] B, // Element B (row 1, column 2)
    input [3:0] C, // Element C (row 2, column 1)
    input [3:0] D, // Element D (row 2, column 2)
    output reg [3:0] A_inv, // Inverse Element A
    output reg [3:0] B_inv, // Inverse Element B
    output reg [3:0] C_inv, // Inverse Element C
    output reg [3:0] D_inv // Inverse Element D
);
    wire [3:0] det; // Determinant
    assign det = A * D - B * C; // Calculate determinant

    always @(*) begin
        if (det != 0) begin
            A_inv = D / det; // A_inv = D/det
            B_inv = -B / det; // B_inv = -B/det
            C_inv = -C / det; // C_inv = -C/det
            D_inv = A / det; // D_inv = A/det
        end else begin
            A_inv = 4'b0000; // Not invertible
            B_inv = 4'b0000;
            C_inv = 4'b0000;
            D_inv = 4'b0000;
        end
    end
endmodule

Each channel will have a request signal (req), an acknowledge signal (ack), and a data output (data_out). The controller should prioritize channel requests in a round-robin manner.
code:
module dma_controller (
    input clk,
    input [3:0] req, // Request signals for 4 channels
    output reg [3:0] ack, // Acknowledge signals for 4 channels
    output reg [7:0] data_out // Data output
);
    reg [1:0] current_channel;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        // Round-robin channel selection
        if (req != 4'b0000) begin
            ack <= 4'b0000; // Clear ack signals
            current_channel <= (current_channel + 1) % 4; // Next channel
            if (req[current_channel]) begin
                ack[current_channel] <= 1'b1; // Acknowledge the current channel
                data_out <= 8'hFF; // Example data output
            end
        end else begin
            ack <= 4'b0000; // No requests, clear ack
        end
    end
endmodule
